expectedText:
MANUFACTURED HOME OWNERSHIP AND TITLE TRANSFER — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jane Doe · John Smith

PURPOSE OF THIS MANUFACTURED HOME OWNERSHIP AND TITLE TRANSFER INFORMATION SHEET
This Information Sheet describes California's statutory system for registering a manufactured home or mobilehome and transferring ownership of it as personal property with the Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) -- HCD's certificate-of-title system, comparable in structure to vehicle titling with the Department of Motor Vehicles. It concerns the home described as 1998 Skyline single-wide manufactured home, bearing HCD serial and/or insignia identification serial no. XXXXXXX, insignia no. XXXXXX, situated at 123 Main St., Space 45, as between Jane Doe as the transferring registered owner and John Smith as the incoming registered owner. This document addresses a different subject than this corpus's separate Mobilehome Park Tenancy (Mobilehome Residency Law) Information Sheet: that document describes the landlord-tenant relationship between a mobilehome resident and the park that rents the underlying space -- the rental agreement, park rules, and statutory grounds for terminating the tenancy -- and says nothing about who owns the home itself or how that ownership changes hands. This Information Sheet, by contrast, addresses only ownership of the home and the transfer of title to it, independent of any space-rental relationship the home may also be subject to. This Information Sheet is further limited to a manufactured home or mobilehome that remains registered as personal property with HCD. A manufactured home that has instead been installed on a foundation system and converted into a fixture or improvement to the real property it sits on leaves this HCD registration and title system entirely and, from that point on, changes hands through the real property recording system instead -- a distinct process not covered by this Information Sheet. This is a general informational reference describing the statutory registration and title-transfer system; it is not itself a certificate of title, an application for registration, a bill of sale, escrow instructions, or a determination that any specific home is currently registered as personal property, has instead become part of the real estate, or has been lawfully transferred.

"MANUFACTURED HOME" AND "MOBILEHOME": TWO AGE-BASED STATUTORY TERMS FOR THE SAME KIND OF STRUCTURE
California's manufactured-housing title and registration statute (Health and Safety Code, Division 13, Part 2) uses two separately defined terms for what a lay reader might informally call a mobile home, distinguished by construction date rather than by function. Section 18007(a) defines "manufactured home" as a structure built on or after June 15, 1976: "'Manufactured home,' for the purposes of this part, means a structure that was constructed on or after June 15, 1976, is transportable in one or more sections, is eight body feet or more in width, or 40 body feet or more in length, in the traveling mode, or, when erected on site, is 320 or more square feet, is built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used as a single-family dwelling with or without a foundation when connected to the required utilities, and includes the plumbing, heating, air conditioning, and electrical systems contained therein." Section 18008(a) defines "mobilehome" in nearly identical terms, but for a structure built before that date: "'Mobilehome,' for the purposes of this part, means a structure that was constructed prior to June 15, 1976, is transportable in one or more sections, is eight body feet or more in width, or 40 body feet or more in length, in the traveling mode, or, when erected onsite, is 320 or more square feet, is built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used as a single-family dwelling with or without a foundation system when connected to the required utilities, and includes the plumbing, heating, air conditioning, and electrical systems contained therein." The June 15, 1976 dividing line corresponds to the effective date of the federal construction and safety standards referenced in both definitions; a manufactured home and a mobilehome are registered, titled, and transferred under the identical statutory procedures described in the remainder of this document.

  "“Mobilehome,” for the purposes of this part, means a structure that was constructed prior to June 15, 1976, is transportable in one or more sections, is eight body feet or more in width, or 40 body feet or more in length, in the traveling mode, or, when erected onsite, is 320 or more square feet, is built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used as a single-family dwelling with or without a foundation system when connected to the required utilities, and includes the plumbing, heating, air conditioning, and electrical systems contained therein."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 18008(a) (California Legislative Information text), Health & Saf. C. § 18008(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=18008.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only the core structural sentence from each subdivision; both § 18007 and § 18008 continue with an additional inclusion for a structure that meets all listed requirements except size where the manufacturer voluntarily certifies compliance with the referenced federal standards, and each section's subdivision (b) separately addresses how the defined term should be read when other statutes use it -- neither elaboration is reproduced here. Two independently numbered sections are treated as two separate sources, not one. This is one state's statute, offered as real evidence of California's own definitions for these terms -- not a claim about which state's law governs any specific structure; other states classify and title factory-built housing differently, and some do not use a 1976 construction-date dividing line at all. This document does not address a "commercial coach," "floating home," "truck camper," or "recreational vehicle," each separately defined elsewhere in this same statute and each subject to its own variations on the registration and title system described in the remainder of this document.

THE GENERAL REGISTRATION REQUIREMENT, AND ITS TRIGGER ON SALE OR TRANSFER OF TITLE
Health and Safety Code section 18075(a) makes titling and registration with the department the general rule for a manufactured home or mobilehome: "Except as provided in Section 18075.7, all manufactured homes, mobilehomes, commercial coaches, truck campers, and floating homes shall be subject to the provisions of this code for the purposes of titling and registration." Section 18075.5 makes that registration an ongoing, annual obligation rather than a one-time event: "Manufactured homes, mobilehomes, commercial coaches, and floating homes sold or used within this state shall be subject to annual registration with the department and payment of registration fees prescribed by Section 18114 except as follows:" Subdivision (a) of that same section then ties registration specifically to a sale of a home not installed on a foundation system: it is subject to registration and fee payment "at the time of original registration with the department, and upon subsequent sale, resale, or transfer of title," and the statute defines a covered "transfer of title" broadly, so that it "includes, but is not limited to, any change, addition, or deletion of one or more registered owners, legal owners, or junior lienholders."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Except as provided in Section 18075.7, all manufactured homes, mobilehomes, commercial coaches, truck campers, and floating homes shall be subject to the provisions of this code for the purposes of titling and registration."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 18075(a) (California Legislative Information text), Health & Saf. C. § 18075(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=18075.)
  "Manufactured homes, mobilehomes, commercial coaches, and floating homes sold or used within this state shall be subject to annual registration with the department and payment of registration fees prescribed by Section 18114 except as follows:"
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 18075.5 (California Legislative Information text), Health & Saf. C. § 18075.5 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=18075.5.)

For purposes of this section, a transfer of title includes, but is not limited to, any change, addition, or deletion of one or more registered owners, legal owners, or junior lienholders."

  Known gap: "The department" in this chapter is the Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD); this clause does not reproduce § 18075(b)'s separate account of HCD's transition into a role for this title and registration system previously held in part by the Department of Motor Vehicles. Section 18075(a)'s own cross-referenced exception (§ 18075.7) and § 18075.5's further exceptions in subdivisions (c) through (f) -- covering homes newly entering California, active-duty and recently discharged military members, and new, unoccupied dealer inventory -- are not reproduced here. This clause treats two independently numbered sections (18075 and 18075.5) as two separate sources; the two quotations drawn from § 18075.5 (its introductory sentence and subdivision (a)) are treated as one source. This is one state's statute, offered as real evidence of California's own registration requirement -- not a claim about which state's law governs any specific home; registration and titling schemes for factory-built housing vary by state.

WHERE THIS HCD TITLE SYSTEM STOPS: A HOME CONVERTED TO REAL PROPERTY
The HCD registration and title system described in this Information Sheet applies only for as long as a manufactured home or mobilehome remains personal property. Health and Safety Code section 18075.5(b) exempts a home installed on a foundation system from this registration system entirely, for as long as it stays affixed: "Manufactured homes, mobilehomes, and commercial coaches installed or to be installed on foundation systems pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 18551 shall be exempt from registration so long as they remain affixed to the foundation system. In the event that the manufactured home, mobilehome, or commercial coach, is removed from a foundation system for any purpose other than dismantling or reinstallation on a foundation system, it shall be immediately subject to registration with the department." Section 18551, which governs foundation systems, confirms that installation on a foundation system presents a genuine either/or choice between two different legal statuses, not a matter of degree: "A manufactured home, mobilehome, or commercial modular may be installed on a foundation system as either a fixture or improvement to the real property, in accordance with subdivision (a), or a manufactured home or mobilehome may be installed on a foundation system as a chattel, in accordance with subdivision (b)." For the fixture-or-improvement path, § 18551(a)(2)(A) identifies the specific document that completes the conversion to real property and where it must be filed -- not with HCD, but with the county recorder: "Within five business days of the issuance of the certificate of occupancy for the manufactured home, mobilehome, or commercial modular by the appropriate enforcement agency, the enforcement agency shall record a document naming the owner of the real property, describing the real property with certainty, and stating that a manufactured home, mobilehome, or commercial modular has been affixed to that real property by installation on a foundation system pursuant to this subdivision. The document shall be recorded with the county recorder of the county where the real property, upon which the manufactured home, mobilehome, or commercial modular that has been installed, is situated." Once that recorded document exists, the home has left HCD's certificate-of-title system described in the remainder of this Information Sheet and instead changes hands, like other real property, through the county recording system; a home installed as a chattel under § 18551(b) instead remains within the HCD title system this Information Sheet describes.

This is one state's statute, offered as real evidence of California's own personal-property/real-property dividing line for a manufactured home -- not a claim about which state's law governs any specific home, and not a determination that any specific home in fact remains chattel or has in fact become real property.

REGISTERED OWNER, LEGAL OWNER, AND JUNIOR LIENHOLDER: THE THREE ROLES ON AN HCD TITLE RECORD
HCD's title record for a manufactured home or mobilehome, like a Department of Motor Vehicles vehicle title record, can name up to three distinct roles rather than a single "owner." Section 18009.5 defines the possessory owner: "'Registered owner' means a person registered by the department as the owner of a manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, floating home, or truck camper." Section 18005.8 defines a first-position secured party: "'Legal owner' means a person holding a security interest in a manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, floating home, or truck camper perfected by filing the appropriate documents with the department pursuant to Section 18080.7 if the person is entitled to the designation, as provided in Article 3 (commencing with Section 18085) or 4 (commencing with Section 18098) of Chapter 8." Section 18005.3 defines a subordinate secured party: "'Junior lienholder' means a person, other than a legal owner, holding a security interest in a manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, floating home, or truck camper perfected by filing the appropriate documents with the department pursuant to Section 18080.7." A home with an outstanding loan against it will typically show a registered owner and a legal owner (the lender) on the same title record, and may show one or more junior lienholders behind the legal owner as well.

  Known gap: This clause reproduces the core definitions of all three roles but does not reproduce § 18005.8's own carve-out (a lien created under a different section, § 18080.9, does not itself make its holder a "legal owner" for purposes of this definition) or the perfection mechanics of § 18080.7 that all three definitions cross-reference, none of which this document independently describes. This is one state's statute, offered as real evidence of California's own three-role structure for a manufactured home title record -- not a claim about which state's law governs any specific home's title, and not a claim that title records for other kinds of property (including an ordinary vehicle title, which this clause draws an analogy to only for orientation) use identical role definitions or the identical department.

APPLYING FOR ORIGINAL HCD REGISTRATION AND TITLE: WHAT THE APPLICATION MUST CONTAIN
Health and Safety Code section 18085 sets the baseline procedure for putting a manufactured home or mobilehome onto HCD's title record for the first time. Subdivision (a) requires a department-approved application accompanied by the manufacturer's certificate of origin: "Application for the original registration of a manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home required to be registered under this part shall be made to the department upon the appropriate forms approved by the department, and shall be accompanied by the filing fee prescribed by the department." Subdivision (b)(4) then requires the application to identify the specific structure by its manufacturer, date of manufacture, and serial and label or insignia numbers -- the same kind of identifiers a vehicle title uses a VIN for: "A description of the manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home, including all of the following: (A) The manufacturer's name and identification number. (B) The date of manufacture. (C) The serial number or numbers. (D) The federal label number or numbers affixed pursuant to the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 5401 et seq.) or department insignia number or numbers affixed pursuant to Section 18026."

This is one state's statute, offered as real evidence of California's own original-registration procedure -- not a claim about which state's law governs any specific home's original registration, and not a determination that any specific application would be accepted or rejected.

TRANSFERRING TITLE ON A SALE: THE CERTIFICATE OF TITLE EXECUTION PROCESS
Health and Safety Code section 18100.5(a) sets out what must happen with HCD once a manufactured home or mobilehome already on the title record changes ownership. The statute requires notice to the department within 20 days: "If the title or interest of a registered owner, legal owner, junior lienholder in a manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, or truck camper, or floating home for which an original registration under this part has been obtained is transferred to another person, or, if all outstanding secured obligations previously held by a legal owner registered on the original or a subsequent registration or by a junior lienholder are satisfied and the person no longer has any obligation to extend credit, incur obligations, or otherwise give value to be secured by the manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home, or, if a security interest is taken in a manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home after the permanent title record has been established, the department shall be notified within 20 days." Paragraph (1) then describes the specific mechanism for an ownership sale -- execution of the existing certificate of title itself by both parties, followed by HCD's issuance of a new one: "If the title or interest of a registered owner or legal owner is being transferred, the transferor and the transferee of the title or interest shall execute in the manner prescribed by the department the certificate of title for the manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home." The statute goes on to require the executed certificate of title, with supporting documents and fees, to be forwarded to HCD, which then amends the permanent title record and issues a new certificate of title and an amended registration card reflecting the change.

WHOSE SIGNATURE TRANSFERS TITLE WHEN A HOME HAS MORE THAN ONE REGISTERED OWNER
Health and Safety Code section 18080 allows a manufactured home or mobilehome to be registered to more than one person, and fixes different signature rules for transferring title depending on the form of co-ownership chosen. For joint tenancy, every joint tenant's signature is required to transfer title, and a deceased joint tenant's interest passes automatically to the survivors: "A manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home may be registered in the names of two or more persons as joint tenants. Upon the death of a joint tenant, the interest of the decedent shall pass to the survivor or survivors. The signature of each joint tenant or survivor or survivors, as the case may be, shall be required to transfer or encumber the title to the manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home." For registration as community property between spouses, both spouses' signatures are required: "A manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home may be registered as community property in the names of the spouses. The signature of each spouse shall be required to transfer or encumber the title to the manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home."

This is one state's statute, offered as real evidence of California's own signature rules for co-owned manufactured home title -- not a claim about which state's law governs any specific home's co-ownership, and not a determination of how any specific home is currently registered or whether every signature required by this statute has in fact been obtained.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF RECEIPT OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
Jane Doe and John Smith each acknowledge receipt of this Manufactured Home Ownership and Title Transfer Information Sheet, describing California's statutory system for HCD registration and title transfer of the manufactured home or mobilehome identified above, and acknowledge that it is a general informational reference rather than a certificate of title, a completed HCD application, a bill of sale, or a legal or tax determination applicable to their specific transaction. Signed at Fresno, California on January 1, 2026.

This is a general informational reference describing the statutory registration and title-transfer system; it is not itself a certificate of title, an application for registration, a bill of sale, escrow instructions, or a determination that any specific home is currently registered as personal property, has instead become part of the real estate, or has been lawfully transferred.

California's manufactured-housing title and registration statute (Health and Safety Code, Division 13, Part 2) uses two separately defined terms for what a lay reader might informally call a mobile home, distinguished by construction date rather than by function. Section 18007(a) defines "manufactured home" as a structure built on or after June 15, 1976: "'Manufactured home,' for the purposes of this part, means a structure that was constructed on or after June 15, 1976, is transportable in one or more sections, is eight body feet or more in width, or 40 body feet or more in length, in the traveling mode, or, when erected on site, is 320 or more square feet, is built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used as a single-family dwelling with or without a foundation when connected to the required utilities, and includes the plumbing, heating, air conditioning, and electrical systems contained therein." Section 18008(a) defines "mobilehome" in nearly identical terms, but for a structure built before that date: "'Mobilehome,' for the purposes of this part, means a structure that was constructed prior to June 15, 1976, is transportable in one or more sections, is eight body feet or more in width, or 40 body feet or more in length, in the traveling mode, or, when erected onsite, is 320 or more square feet, is built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used as a single-family dwelling with or without a foundation system when connected to the required utilities, and includes the plumbing, heating, air conditioning, and electrical systems contained therein." The June 15, 1976 dividing line corresponds to the effective date of the federal construction and safety standards referenced in both definitions; a manufactured home and a mobilehome are registered, titled, and transferred under the identical statutory procedures described in the remainder of this document.

This document does not address a "commercial coach," "floating home," "truck camper," or "recreational vehicle," each separately defined elsewhere in this same statute and each subject to its own variations on the registration and title system described in the remainder of this document.

expectedJSON.body: Health and Safety Code section 18075(a) makes titling and registration with the department the general rule for a manufactured home or mobilehome: "Except as provided in Section 18075.7, all manufactured homes, mobilehomes, commercial coaches, truck campers, and floating homes shall be subject to the provisions of this code for the purposes of titling and registration." Section 18075.5 makes that registration an ongoing, annual obligation rather than a one-time event: "Manufactured homes, mobilehomes, commercial coaches, and floating homes sold or used within this state shall be subject to annual registration with the department and payment of registration fees prescribed by Section 18114 except as follows:" Subdivision (a) of that same section then ties registration specifically to a sale of a home not installed on a foundation system: it is subject to registration and fee payment "at the time of original registration with the department, and upon subsequent sale, resale, or transfer of title," and the statute defines a covered "transfer of title" broadly, so that it "includes, but is not limited to, any change, addition, or deletion of one or more registered owners, legal owners, or junior lienholders."

expectedJSON.body: The HCD registration and title system described in this Information Sheet applies only for as long as a manufactured home or mobilehome remains personal property. Health and Safety Code section 18075.5(b) exempts a home installed on a foundation system from this registration system entirely, for as long as it stays affixed: "Manufactured homes, mobilehomes, and commercial coaches installed or to be installed on foundation systems pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 18551 shall be exempt from registration so long as they remain affixed to the foundation system. In the event that the manufactured home, mobilehome, or commercial coach, is removed from a foundation system for any purpose other than dismantling or reinstallation on a foundation system, it shall be immediately subject to registration with the department." Section 18551, which governs foundation systems, confirms that installation on a foundation system presents a genuine either/or choice between two different legal statuses, not a matter of degree: "A manufactured home, mobilehome, or commercial modular may be installed on a foundation system as either a fixture or improvement to the real property, in accordance with subdivision (a), or a manufactured home or mobilehome may be installed on a foundation system as a chattel, in accordance with subdivision (b)." For the fixture-or-improvement path, § 18551(a)(2)(A) identifies the specific document that completes the conversion to real property and where it must be filed -- not with HCD, but with the county recorder: "Within five business days of the issuance of the certificate of occupancy for the manufactured home, mobilehome, or commercial modular by the appropriate enforcement agency, the enforcement agency shall record a document naming the owner of the real property, describing the real property with certainty, and stating that a manufactured home, mobilehome, or commercial modular has been affixed to that real property by installation on a foundation system pursuant to this subdivision. The document shall be recorded with the county recorder of the county where the real property, upon which the manufactured home, mobilehome, or commercial modular that has been installed, is situated." Once that recorded document exists, the home has left HCD's certificate-of-title system described in the remainder of this Information Sheet and instead changes hands, like other real property, through the county recording system; a home installed as a chattel under § 18551(b) instead remains within the HCD title system this Information Sheet describes.

This clause also does not address what happens to a certificate of title already on file with HCD once the county-recorded document is filed, nor the reverse process for later removing the home from the foundation system and returning it to HCD registration, both of which this document does not cover. This clause draws three quotations from two independently numbered sections (18075.5 and 18551); the two quotations from § 18551 (its opening fixture/chattel sentence and subdivision (a)(2)(A)) are treated as one source. This is one state's statute, offered as real evidence of California's own personal-property/real-property dividing line for a manufactured home -- not a claim about which state's law governs any specific home, and not a determination that any specific home in fact remains chattel or has in fact become real property.

expectedJSON.body: HCD's title record for a manufactured home or mobilehome, like a Department of Motor Vehicles vehicle title record, can name up to three distinct roles rather than a single "owner." Section 18009.5 defines the possessory owner: "'Registered owner' means a person registered by the department as the owner of a manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, floating home, or truck camper." Section 18005.8 defines a first-position secured party: "'Legal owner' means a person holding a security interest in a manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, floating home, or truck camper perfected by filing the appropriate documents with the department pursuant to Section 18080.7 if the person is entitled to the designation, as provided in Article 3 (commencing with Section 18085) or 4 (commencing with Section 18098) of Chapter 8." Section 18005.3 defines a subordinate secured party: "'Junior lienholder' means a person, other than a legal owner, holding a security interest in a manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, floating home, or truck camper perfected by filing the appropriate documents with the department pursuant to Section 18080.7." A home with an outstanding loan against it will typically show a registered owner and a legal owner (the lender) on the same title record, and may show one or more junior lienholders behind the legal owner as well.

expectedJSON.body: Health and Safety Code section 18085 sets the baseline procedure for putting a manufactured home or mobilehome onto HCD's title record for the first time. Subdivision (a) requires a department-approved application accompanied by the manufacturer's certificate of origin: "Application for the original registration of a manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home required to be registered under this part shall be made to the department upon the appropriate forms approved by the department, and shall be accompanied by the filing fee prescribed by the department." Subdivision (b)(4) then requires the application to identify the specific structure by its manufacturer, date of manufacture, and serial and label or insignia numbers -- the same kind of identifiers a vehicle title uses a VIN for: "A description of the manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home, including all of the following: (A) The manufacturer's name and identification number. (B) The date of manufacture. (C) The serial number or numbers. (D) The federal label number or numbers affixed pursuant to the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 5401 et seq.) or department insignia number or numbers affixed pursuant to Section 18026."

expectedJSON.body: Health and Safety Code section 18100.5(a) sets out what must happen with HCD once a manufactured home or mobilehome already on the title record changes ownership. The statute requires notice to the department within 20 days: "If the title or interest of a registered owner, legal owner, junior lienholder in a manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, or truck camper, or floating home for which an original registration under this part has been obtained is transferred to another person, or, if all outstanding secured obligations previously held by a legal owner registered on the original or a subsequent registration or by a junior lienholder are satisfied and the person no longer has any obligation to extend credit, incur obligations, or otherwise give value to be secured by the manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home, or, if a security interest is taken in a manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home after the permanent title record has been established, the department shall be notified within 20 days." Paragraph (1) then describes the specific mechanism for an ownership sale -- execution of the existing certificate of title itself by both parties, followed by HCD's issuance of a new one: "If the title or interest of a registered owner or legal owner is being transferred, the transferor and the transferee of the title or interest shall execute in the manner prescribed by the department the certificate of title for the manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home." The statute goes on to require the executed certificate of title, with supporting documents and fees, to be forwarded to HCD, which then amends the permanent title record and issues a new certificate of title and an amended registration card reflecting the change.

expectedJSON.body: Health and Safety Code section 18080 allows a manufactured home or mobilehome to be registered to more than one person, and fixes different signature rules for transferring title depending on the form of co-ownership chosen. For joint tenancy, every joint tenant's signature is required to transfer title, and a deceased joint tenant's interest passes automatically to the survivors: "A manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home may be registered in the names of two or more persons as joint tenants. Upon the death of a joint tenant, the interest of the decedent shall pass to the survivor or survivors. The signature of each joint tenant or survivor or survivors, as the case may be, shall be required to transfer or encumber the title to the manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home." For registration as community property between spouses, both spouses' signatures are required: "A manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home may be registered as community property in the names of the spouses. The signature of each spouse shall be required to transfer or encumber the title to the manufactured home, mobilehome, commercial coach, truck camper, or floating home."
